# Tap twice to mute your mic. Tap three times to play music. Tap four times to pick from a menu. Tap twice. Mute your mic.

Knucklebop turns the motion sensor already inside your MacBook into invisible buttons. Tap the palm rest, or the desk right next to it, two to six times, and your Mac does something different for each count, in each app.

## A tap is a button. The count is which one.

### Tap the palm rest or desk

Two to six light taps beside the trackpad, or on the desk next to your MacBook. Your timing doesn't matter, just the count.

### Your Mac does it

A small pill confirms what happened. One stray bump never counts.

## Try it right here.

Pick an app, then click the palm rest (or focus it and press Space) a few times. This is exactly how the app decides what to do.

### Rules in Zoom

Website rules beat app rules, and app rules beat "anywhere" rules. One pattern per tap count.

## What can a tap do? Almost anything.

Pick from ready-made actions, or point a tap at any shortcut, automation or script.

results.title: This Free App Unlocks A Useful Tap Feature On Your MacBook's Palm Rest
results.content:
X/Jaskirat Singh

Available for download from the developer's website or from GitHub, MacTap supports two types of gestures. If you're holding the laptop on your lap, you may want to tap on the palm rest to perform a specific shortcut. If the laptop sits still on a desk, tapping on the desk may be even more convenient, as the knock would reverberate through the chassis. The GitHub documentation says that MacTap will work on MacBook Air (M2 and later) and MacBook Pro (M1 Pro, M1 Max, and later) models, as motion sensor data has to be available to apps. That way, the software can listen for and interpret motions like taps and knocks and pair them with actions. [...] MacBooks don't have a native equivalent to Back Tap, and that's understandable. Interacting with a laptop may be even easier than interacting with a smartphone, as you have access to the trackpad, a full keyboard, and powerful keyboard shortcuts to help you control apps and multitask with speed. Also, the Back Tap name would not make sense, as tapping the back of the lid or the bottom side of the case would be cumbersome. That's why apps like MacTap, released in early September 2026, use the palm rest for taps.
